newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Air to find partner despite loss.
newsitem.headline: Saab Air to find partner despite loss.

text.p: Swedish aircraft maker Saab Aircraft AB said on Thursday it does not expect its parent company's 1996 loss to decrease its chances of finding a partner.
"I do not think these figures will worsen the chances of finding a partner," Bengt Halse, the chief executive of Saab AB, told a news conference.
Saab Aircraft AB is fully owned by Saab AB.
Saab said on Thursday its 1996 operating loss deepened to 1.40 billion crowns ($187.9 million) from 354 million in 1995.
Halse said Saab is discussing cooperation with possible partners, but he did not want to say when cooperation could start.
"It takes two to tango," he said.
Saab Aircraft has no intention of stepping out of the 2000 model program, Halse added.
Saab AB is held by investment company Investor AB, the key holding company in the Wallenberg family's financial empire.
